### SI joint & its ligaments
- SI joint → front-lower part **synovial** (auricular surface) · back-upper part **fibrous** (iliac tuberosity)
  [[FIG: Fig 6.5 · 6.02
- **Interosseous SI ligament** → **vertical** stability · **posterior SI** → very strong · **anterior SI** → thin, torn first in open book

PITFALL — strongest SI ligament
- Netter → **posterior** SI · SI anatomy notes → **interosseous** ("strongest in the body")
- Say → "**the posterior complex — interosseous and posterior SI — is the strongest**"

|---|---|---|
| **Horizontal** | Rotational (stops opening) | Anterior SI, iliolumbar, **sacrospinous** |

6.07.t: Blood Supply of the Femoral Head & Anastomoses
6.07.b:
### The chain — from profunda to the dome
1) **Profunda femoris** → **MFCA** (medial femoral circumflex artery, posterior) + **LFCA** (lateral femoral circumflex artery, anterior)
[[FIG: Fig 6.27, 6.28 · 6.07
2) → **extracapsular ring** at the base of the neck
3) → **ascending cervical (retinacular) arteries** under the synovium along the neck
4) → **subsynovial ring** at the edge of the head
5) → **epiphyseal arteries** → the **lateral epiphyseal** (from the MFCA, posterosuperior) feeds the **weight-bearing dome**

- **Artery of ligamentum teres** (obturator) → small medial area near the fovea in adults
- LFCA → mainly the **anterior neck** + greater trochanter in adults

CLINICAL PEARL — why the displaced neck fracture fails
- Retinacular vessels run **inside the capsule on the posterosuperior neck** → a displaced neck fracture tears them (Nagah p12)
- Result → **AVN** (avascular necrosis) + **nonunion** · intertrochanteric = extracapsular, cancellous, well fed → heals

### MFCA deep branch — the surgeon's artery
- Runs between **pectineus and iliopsoas** → behind the neck **under quadratus femoris**
  [[FIG: Fig 6.29, 6.30 · 6.07
- Crosses **behind obturator externus** → then **in front of the conjoint tendon** (gemelli + obturator internus)
- Pierces the capsule at **gemellus superior** → retinacular vessels on the **posterosuperior neck** · **obturator externus protects it** in any dislocation

CLINICAL PEARL — saving the MFCA
- Posterior approach → cut the rotators **off the bone**, keep **obturator externus** intact
- Neck fracture fixed in **too much valgus** → stretches the MFCA → AVN (Nagah p12)

### Supply by age
[[FIG: Fig 6.31 · 6.07
| Age | Main supply |
|---|---|
| **0–4 y** | MFCA + LFCA + ligamentum teres artery · metaphyseal vessels still cross |
| **4–8 y** | **MFCA almost alone** → physis blocks metaphyseal vessels · ligamentum teres not yet working |
| **>8 y** | MFCA predominant · ligamentum teres adds a little |

- 4–8 y window → **peak Perthes risk**

PITFALL — ligamentum teres artery after 8 years
- Handbook → contributes **after 8 y** · Netter → "minimal supply to the adult head"
- Say → "**it helps a little after about 8 years, never enough to save the head after a displaced neck fracture**"

### Trochanteric & cruciate anastomoses
[[FIG: Fig 6.32, 6.33 · 6.07
| Anastomosis | Where | Vessels |
|---|---|---|
| **Trochanteric** | Trochanteric fossa | Superior gluteal (descending) · inferior gluteal · ascending branches of MFCA + LFCA |
| **Cruciate** | Behind the femur at the **lesser trochanter**, under quadratus femoris | **Inferior gluteal** (above) · **1st perforator** (below) · transverse branches of **MFCA** (medial) + **LFCA** (lateral) |

MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "anastomoses around the hip"
- Two rings → **trochanteric** (at the fossa) feeds the neck · **cruciate** (at the lesser trochanter) links pelvis to thigh
- Trochanteric → superior + inferior gluteal + ascending MFCA and LFCA
- Cruciate → a cross: inferior gluteal above, 1st perforator below, MFCA medial, LFCA lateral
- Value → **internal iliac ↔ femoral system** bypass if the femoral artery is blocked above the profunda

6.07.1.t: The chain — from profunda to the dome
6.07.1.b:
1) **Profunda femoris** → **MFCA** (medial femoral circumflex artery, posterior) + **LFCA** (lateral femoral circumflex artery, anterior)

CLINICAL PEARL — why the displaced neck fracture fails
- Retinacular vessels run **inside the capsule on the posterosuperior neck** → a displaced neck fracture tears them (Nagah p12)
- Result → **AVN** (avascular necrosis) + **nonunion** · intertrochanteric = extracapsular, cancellous, well fed → heals

6.07.2.t: MFCA deep branch — the surgeon's artery
6.07.2.b:
- Runs between **pectineus and iliopsoas** → behind the neck **under quadratus femoris**
  [[FIG: Fig 6.29, 6.30 · 6.07
- Crosses **behind obturator externus** → then **in front of the conjoint tendon** (gemelli + obturator internus)
- Pierces the capsule at **gemellus superior** → retinacular vessels on the **posterosuperior neck** · **obturator externus protects it** in any dislocation

CLINICAL PEARL — saving the MFCA
- Posterior approach → cut the rotators **off the bone**, keep **obturator externus** intact
- Neck fracture fixed in **too much valgus** → stretches the MFCA → AVN (Nagah p12)

### Superior gluteal nerve — the safe zone
- Runs **between gluteus medius and minimus** → inferior branch ends in **TFL**
  [[FIG: Fig 6.46, 6.47 · 6.11

PITFALL — 5 cm or 3 cm?
- Bos 1994 → **3 cm** · Abdel Azeem → lower **third** of the greater trochanter-to-crest distance
- Say → "**classic 5 cm, but the lowest branch can be at 3 cm → stay low and split in line with the fibres**"

### Sciatic, femoral, obturator, LFCN
[[FIG: Fig 6.48 · 6.11
- **Sciatic** → two parts in one sheath → split near the popliteal fossa · **femoral** → **saphenous** to the medial leg · **obturator** → inferomedial thigh skin
- **LFCN** → lateral thigh skin only · exits ≈**1.9 cm medial to the ASIS** → keep ≥3 cm away

- **Peroneal division** → hurt more, recovers less → **tethered at the notch**
- Knee flexion **relaxes** the sciatic nerve · THA (total hip arthroplasty) lengthening >3.5–4 cm → sciatic risk

### Arteries
- **Internal iliac** → posterior division → **superior gluteal** (at the notch) · anterior division → obturator, inferior gluteal, internal pudendal
  [[FIG: Fig 6.49, 6.50, 6.51 · 6.11
- Pelvic fracture bleeding → **venous** commonest (presacral plexus) · **arterial 15%** (superior gluteal, internal pudendal)
- **LFCA** → ascending (to the neck, crosses the anterior approach) · transverse (to the greater trochanter) · descending (to the knee)

MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "corona mortis"
- "Crown of death" → vessel joining the **obturator** (internal iliac) to the **inferior epigastric / external iliac**
- Lies **behind the superior pubic ramus**, ≈**6 cm** from the symphysis (range 4–10 cm) (Okcu 2004; Darmanis 2007)
- Any vessel ≈60–80% (mostly **veins**); **artery** ≈1 in 5 (Okcu 2004)
- Cut → retracts into the obturator foramen → bleeding hard to stop
- Found and tied in the **ilioinguinal medial window** and **Stoppa** approaches

PITFALL — how common is the corona mortis?
- Handbook → 10–15% · Campbell → >80%
- Say → "**arterial in about 1 in 5, a vein in most** → look for it in every anterior approach"

HIGH YIELD — what is at risk, by region
- Iliac crest graft → front **LFCN** (start ≥3 cm behind the ASIS) · back **superior cluneal nerves** + superior gluteal artery (notch)
- Pelvic fixation → **L5 root** + superior gluteal bundle (iliosacral screw) · **lumbosacral trunk** (anterior SI plate) · **corona mortis** + external iliac vessels, femoral nerve, obturator bundle (ilioinguinal / Stoppa)
- Cup screws → posterosuperior **safe** (too long → sciatic, superior gluteal) · posteroinferior caution, ≤20 mm (bone ≈25 mm) · anterosuperior **death** (external iliac vessels) · anteroinferior danger (obturator bundle)
- Hip arthroscopy → anterior portal **LFCN** (≈3 mm away; hit in 38%) · anterolateral → **superior gluteal nerve** ≈4.4 cm · posterolateral → **sciatic** ≈2.9 cm · traction post → **pudendal**
- THA → posterior **sciatic** (peroneal division) + MFCA · direct lateral **superior gluteal nerve** (6.11) · anterior **LFCN**, nerve to TFL, ascending LFCA

- Cup-screw lines → line 1 **ASIS through the acetabular centre**, line 2 perpendicular → "**back is safe, front kills**"
- Retractor under the transverse ligament → **obturator nerve** just below the notch · over the anterior wall → **femoral nerve**, superficial to iliocapsularis
- THA nerve injury ≈1% → sciatic commonest · lateral → superior gluteal · anterior → LFCN
- Approach-by-approach dangers → 6B
